proof_skeleton_nl: Fix a coloring f : R^2 -> {red,green} satisfying the stated circumcenter condition. By L1, each color class is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples. By L2, some color class S_c contains an equilateral triangle. By L3, that implies S_c is not contained in a line. The same triangle also shows S_c is nonempty. Therefore S_c satisfies all hypotheses of L5: it is nonempty, circumcenter-closed on noncollinear triples, and not collinear. Hence L5 gives S_c = R^2. Finally, by L6, if one color class is all of R^2, then the coloring is constant, which is exactly the theorem's conclusion.

steps.derives: Under the root hypothesis on f, both color classes R_f = {P | f(P)=red} and G_f = {P | f(P)=green} are closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples of their own points.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the content of L1 after instantiating S first with the red class and then with the green class.

steps.derives: There exist a color c in {red,green} and points A,B,C in R^2 such that A,B,C form an equilateral triangle and f(A)=f(B)=f(C)=c.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L2 directly to the given coloring f.

steps.derives: If S_c denotes the color class {P in R^2 | f(P)=c}, then S_c is not contained in any line.
steps.trivial_justification: By A2, the set S_c contains the three vertices A,B,C of an equilateral triangle. L3 states that any set containing the vertices of an equilateral triangle is not contained in a line.

steps.derives: The color class S_c = {P in R^2 | f(P)=c} is nonempty.
steps.trivial_justification: From A2, the points A,B,C all belong to S_c, so S_c is nonempty.

steps.derives: The color class S_c is closed under circumcenters of noncollinear triples of points from S_c.
steps.trivial_justification: A1 established the circumcenter-closure property for both color classes; in particular it holds for the class S_c.

Not trivial: we combine three previously established properties of S_c. Step A4 gives nonemptiness, Step A5 gives circumcenter-closure on noncollinear triples, and Step A3 gives that S_c is not contained in a line. These are exactly the hypotheses of L5, so L5 yields S_c = R^2.

steps.derives: There exists a color c' in {red,green} such that for every point P in R^2, f(P)=c'.
steps.trivial_justification: Apply L6 to the color c from A2 and the equality S_c = R^2 obtained in A6.
